keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for a state Cliopatria lacks (its Great Jin shape of 1206-1215 covers Liaoning and the 1216 shape drops it). '13th-century kingdom in what is now Northeast China' with its capital at Kaiyuan, Liaoning; 1215: 'Yelu Liuge occupied the eastern capital of the Jin dynasty' (Dongjing, Liaoyang). The page gives no area and no boundary, and no land change after 1215, so Liaoning (218 thousand km2), the reading in the great-jin dossier's 1212 loss, is carried to the end under Mongol vassalage (confidence 1).

ledger.note: 1212: Yelu Liuge's revolt. 'In 1212, the Khitan leader Yelu Liuge rebelled against the Jin and declared his allegiance to Genghis Khan' (Mongol conquest of the Jin page); 'Yelu Liuge rebelled against the rule of the Jurchen-led Jin dynasty in 1212' (Eastern Liao page, which adds that he 'allied himself with Genghis Khan' and the kingdom 'then became a vassalage of the Mongol Empire', both undated); the Eastern Xia page dates his revolt 1211. The land is the researcher's reading of 'Northeast China' round Kaiyuan, Liaoning (confidence 2).
1213: 'Yelu Liuge proclaimed himself king', dynastic name Liao, era name Yuantong (1213-1220).

1214 (the page's paragraph): 'Yelu Liuge established his capital at modern-day Kaiyuan, Liaoning', renamed Zhongjing; the sentence is undated. Kaiyuan is not in the gazetteer, so no capital coordinates are given.

notes:
State Cliopatria lacks (the Jin page lists it as a successor of the Jin). Cliopatria's Great Jin shape of 1206-1215 covers Liaoning and the 1216 shape drops it; this dossier and the eastern-xia dossier explain the drop. The great-jin dossier's 1212 loss of Liaodong names this slug.

Dates and extent. The Eastern Liao page gives 1212 (revolt), 1213 (kingship), 1214 (capital at Kaiyuan, Jin attack), 1215 (Dongjing), 1216 (Sibu's Later Liao), 1219 (Hanshe), 1220 (Liuge's death) and 1269 (title abolished); it gives no territory. The 1269 end is the title's abolition by the Yuan; the kingdom was a Mongol vassal from 1212 (the vassal pair, 1212 to 1269, belongs in the mongol-empire dossier, another group, with this slug as counterpart). The Eastern Xia page dates Liuge's revolt 1211 and the Puxian Wannu page puts Wannu's Eastern Xia in Dongjing in 1215, where the Eastern Liao page has Liuge occupying the Jin's eastern capital. Later Liao (1216-1219, Yelu Sibu) is a counterpart name only; no dossier is written for it. Kaiyuan, Liaoning is not in the gazetteer (no capital coordinates).
